title: The root layout: where every page begins
description: Start at the App Router root layout, the shell that wraps every route. It configures the font and site-wide SEO metadata, injects the Meta Pixel, and renders the persistent header, footer, and animated background that frame all marketing, session, giveaway, and event pages.

title: The home page and the session catalog
description: The home page sorts the session registry and renders it as a staggered animated grid of cards. Look at how sessions.ts acts as the central catalog of the ten workshop sessions and how locks.ts gates which guides, prep, and tools are visible, so you understand the data that drives the participant side of the site.

title: Shared UI and animation building blocks
description: Almost every page composes the same handful of reusable components. Study the scroll reveal and stagger animations, the copyable CodeBlock, the sticky video player, and the Vanta/Three.js hero to see the visual vocabulary that gives marketing and session pages their look and interactivity.

title: Giveaways: the lead-generation funnel
description: Giveaways are the public top of funnel. The registry in giveaways.ts powers an animated index page, while the segment layout wraps each giveaway in a copy-email gate. This is where anonymous visitors first meet the brand and are nudged to hand over an email.

title: Email capture: turning visitors into leads
description: The giveaway pages share three coordinated pieces of lead capture. The reusable email modal collects and submits the address, the copy-email gate blocks copy actions until an email is given, and the auto modal passively opens the capture form on mount. Together they define the conversion mechanic behind every giveaway.

title: The events catalog and event landing pages
description: Events are the paid product. The events.tsx catalog is the single source of truth for event definitions, pricing, and promo helpers, feeding both the events index and the dynamic per-event detail page. The EventPageView renderer composes typed sections into the full landing page that leads to checkout.

title: The checkout domain: Stripe and Supabase wiring
description: These libraries form the commerce core. event-checkout resolves mode and amount and builds Stripe session params, stripe.ts and supabase.ts provide the configured clients, and event-registration-db is the Supabase data layer that saves, counts, and cancels registrations. Understanding this layer is key to following any purchase.

title: The checkout flow end to end
description: Now trace a real purchase. The registration section component drives Stripe embedded checkout, promo codes, donations, and waitlist fallback; the checkout-session API creates the Stripe session with validation and rate limiting; and the Stripe webhook plus finalize-registration routes turn a completed payment into a confirmed registration.

title: Waitlists, promos, and lead-magnet APIs
description: Beyond checkout, several POST routes capture intent and demand. The waitlist join route validates and confirms signups, validate-promo returns discounted pricing, and the lead-magnet and subscribe routes capture emails, deliver assets via Resend, and ingest into the CRM. These are the smaller conversion endpoints that surround the main funnel.

title: Transactional email, calendar links, and signed tokens
description: After a purchase the site sends rich transactional mail. event-confirmation-email builds and sends confirmation, setup, reminder, and waitlist messages via Resend, the calendar library generates iCal and Google Calendar links, and event-tokens issues HMAC-signed links used for secure cancel and cron actions.

title: Abandoned-checkout automation and scheduled jobs
description: Recovering lost sales is fully automated. The followups library handles eligibility, idempotent claim-and-send, and Resend delivery; the cron API route runs the day-1 workflow with per-event window locking; and the CLI script lets operators preview or live-run the same flow. This shows the project's idempotency and locking discipline.

title: The database schema behind it all
description: The SQL migrations define the persistence model everything above relies on. The first migration creates registrations, waitlist, and email rules; the rate-limit and cron-lock migration adds the throttling and concurrency infrastructure; and the abandoned-checkout migration defines automation controls, per-recipient state, and suppression tables.

title: Ops scripts and deployment cron config
description: Operators maintain the system with standalone scripts and Vercel scheduling. The backfill script repairs registrations from paid Stripe sessions, the control script toggles abandoned-checkout automation modes in Supabase, and vercel.json wires the cron schedules and host rewrite that drive the automated jobs in production.

title: Tests and project configuration
description: Finish with the safety net and the toolchain. The test suite covers checkout params, the giveaway email contract, and pricing, while package.json declares the scripts and dependency stack and tailwind.config.ts defines the brand theme. These tie together the conventions seen throughout the tour.
